note: onlyone_admin_toolbar is a bundled glue submodule of onlyone. It has NO configuration, no configure route, no permissions, no drush, no plugin types. It reacts to the parent module's onlyone.settings: hook_menu_links_discovered_alter appends ' (Edit)' to the Admin Toolbar Tools 'Add content' links for restricted content types that already have a node, and (when onlyone_new_menu_entry is on) moves them under the onlyone.add_page parent. It provides the onlyone.admin_toolbar service (rebuildMenu) and an event subscriber on onlyone.content_types_updated. It requires admin_toolbar_tools and onlyone. Because the submodule holds no state of its own, medium/hard cases are grounded in (a) its installation state on the live site and (b) the onlyone.settings.onlyone_node_types config it consumes. Baseline is DISABLED; setup/reset enable it and cleanups uninstall it again (admin_toolbar_tools, pulled in as a dependency, is left as-is). Content-type fixtures are namespaced onlyone_atb_eval / onlyone_atb_task.

evals.prompt: What does the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule do to the Admin Toolbar 'Add content' menu for content types that are configured as Only One?
evals.expected_output: For each Only One content type that already has a node, it appends ' (Edit)' to that type's link in the Admin Toolbar Tools 'Add content' menu (and moves it under 'Add content (Only One)' when that option is enabled), so editors jump straight to editing the existing node.

evals.prompt: Which modules does the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule depend on?
evals.expected_output: It depends on admin_toolbar_tools (Admin Toolbar Extra Tools) and onlyone (its parent module).

evals.prompt: Does the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule have its own configuration/settings page? If not, what configuration drives its behavior?
evals.expected_output: No, it has no configuration of its own. Its behavior is driven entirely by the parent module's onlyone.settings (onlyone_node_types and onlyone_new_menu_entry).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule installed, and what service does it provide for rebuilding the toolbar menu?
evals.expected_output: Yes, onlyone_admin_toolbar is installed; it provides the onlyone.admin_toolbar service (OnlyOneAdminToolbar::rebuildMenu).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule is active. Inspect the live Only One configuration and report which content type its Admin Toolbar integration will annotate (i.e. which type is restricted to one node).
evals.expected_output: onlyone.settings.onlyone_node_types contains 'onlyone_atb_eval', so the toolbar integration acts on that content type.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Only One module is installed and the site uses Admin Toolbar. Install the bundled onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule so the Admin Toolbar 'Add content' menu reflects the Only One restrictions. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The onlyone_admin_toolbar module is installed (drush en onlyone_admin_toolbar -y), which also enables its admin_toolbar_tools dependency.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the onlyone_admin_toolbar submodule is installed. There is a content type 'onlyone_atb_task'. Configure Only One so that this content type is restricted to one node per language, so the Admin Toolbar integration will annotate it. Apply the change to the live site.
